requirement:
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
rationale:
I judged the supplied tests against each clause of `requirements.authoring.invocation`. I found no gap. I did not read any implementation source. The cited `requirements.authoring.refresh` is context only, and I did not reassess its tests.

- **Author one existing requirement or named example.**
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[initial_prompt_substitutes_subject_and_mandatory_inputs_into_the_template]` runs `habeas author` on both a requirement and an example. It checks that the evidence record has `requirement` or `example` set, as the subject's kind requires.
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[author_rejects_unknown_subjects_and_conflicting_targets]` checks that a nonexistent subject fails with its name in stderr and leaves the evidence file unchanged.
- **`--config <name>`.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[an_explicit_configuration_selects_the_nondefault_workspace_profile]` selects a nondefault profile. It asserts that the request used the alternate model and key, and that the usage record shows the alternate model and backend. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[authoring_uses_nearest_workspace_configuration_without_a_user_file]` covers the default (no `--config`) path.
- **Refresh flags in the command form.** `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]` runs `--missing`, `--force`, `--stdout`, and the mutual-exclusion errors, including through the `author-evidence` alias. The refresh semantics are `requirements.authoring.refresh`'s obligations, and that test is also marked for them.
- **`-v` and `--verbose`.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs]` runs both spellings. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` runs `--verbose` together with `--stdout`.
- **Completion report names subject, backend, model, evidence destination and usage path.**
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` asserts that stdout starts with `SUBJECT: ollama / MODEL`. It also asserts an `Evidence:` line whose canonical path equals `evidence/SUBJECT.json`, and a `Usage:` line.
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[initial_prompt_substitutes_subject_and_mandatory_inputs_into_the_template]` repeats these checks for both a requirement and an example. It also asserts that the usage path is an existing file.
- **Destination is stdout when `--stdout` is selected.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` asserts `Evidence: stdout\n` in stderr.
- **Report and diagnostics go to stderr in stdout mode.**
  - In the same test, stdout parses as a single evidence JSON document with exactly the schema's fields. The subject/backend/model line and the usage path appear in stderr. The test also covers the case where no evidence directory exists.
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[missing_duplicate_and_invalid_submissions_preserve_existing_evidence]` runs failures with `--stdout` and asserts that stdout is empty. The failure message ("even after a reminder") is checked in stderr only in the no-submission case, and only without a stdout-versus-file split.
- **`author-evidence` alias.** It is used as the command in `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]`, `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]`, `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[missing_duplicate_and_invalid_submissions_preserve_existing_evidence]`, and in the `--all` conflict check. Those tests assert real outcomes: evidence written, JSON on stdout, and failures.

The helpers `Fixture`, `run` and `command` are marked or reached from marked tests, so there is no marking gap.

text: :::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} refresh
Every `habeas author` form MUST accept `--missing` and `--force`, which are
mutually exclusive; `--missing` MUST be the default. Under `--missing`, the
command MUST assess only the selected subjects whose evidence is missing, stale,
or invalid, and MUST preserve every current record without invoking a model,
including accepted FIXME judgments and current false judgments; a current false
judgment is reassessed only when its subject or inputs change or `--force` is
given. Under `--force`, the command MUST assess every selected subject. `--stdout`
MUST imply `--force`, because it writes no evidence. The command MUST report the
number of selected subjects it skipped as current. When no assessment is needed,
the command MUST succeed without resolving model configuration or credentials.
